correctness.rationale: Independent first-arrival times X_i~Exp(p_i) give density h_i(t)=p_i exp(-p_it)product_{j !=i}(1-exp(-p_jt)) for the unique last new type. The conditional winner law is w_i(t)=q_i(t)/Q(t), where q_i(t)=p_it/(exp(p_it)-1). Given last type i at T=t, its count is one and other independent Poisson counts, truncated above zero, are singleton with Bernoulli probabilities q_j(t). Mixture is exactly positive-size-bias of Poisson-binomial Y_t, P(S=s|T=t)=s[z^s]F_t(z)/Q(t). The sum W of remaining Bernoullis has positive log-concave coefficients a_s; as one q increases, the ratio of size-biased pmfs across q has increasing fractional-linear dependence on a_(s-1)/a_s, including the terminal infinite ratio; hence strict MLR monotonicity in each coordinate. Every q_i(t) decreases strictly, giving strict reverse MLR for 0<t<u. This yields strictly decreasing conditional means of each strictly increasing g and Cov(f(T),g(S))<0 by independent-copy identity. Independently checked explicit convolution p=(.5,.3,.2), t=.5 vs5, obtaining strict increasing earlier/later probability ratios. No discrete stopping-count assertion is made.
